results.title: Staff+ Software Engineer, Deployment
results.location: Remote-Friendly (Travel-Required) | San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA | New York City, NY

output.reasoning: This posting fails on role type, level, and skills fit, though location and sponsorship pass. Role type: 'Staff+ Software Engineer, Deployment' sits in 'Software Engineering - Infrastructure'. The job is building deployment pipelines, progressive delivery, feature flags, runtime configuration, infrastructure-as-code, and artifact distribution. It is not hands-on ML, NLP, or AI systems engineering, and it matches none of Ananya's target roles (Machine Learning Engineer, AI Engineer, Applied NLP Engineer, ML Engineer, Research Engineer). Level: the title says Staff+, and the minimum qualifications require 'Experience leading the design, building, and operation of distributed systems or infrastructure in production, including technical direction across teams'. The $405,000-$485,000 salary also reflects a very senior level. This is not realistic for a new grad finishing an MS at Boston University in 2026-12 whose only experience is an 8-month ML Engineer co-op. Skills fit: the minimum qualifications name more than 2 technologies (Rust, Go, C++, Java, Kubernetes, AWS, GCP). Only AWS is in her shipped list, so fewer than 2 match and the skills test fails. Kubernetes is a core requirement, and she lists it only under familiar_with_not_shipped, which disqualifies on its own under the rules. She has also shipped none of the required backend or systems languages (Rust/Go/C++/Java); her languages are Python and SQL. Location passes: the posting is Remote-Friendly (Travel-Required) with US offices in San Francisco, Seattle, and New York City, and she is willing to relocate within the US. Sponsorship passes: the posting says 'We do sponsor visas!', which matters because she needs sponsorship. These do not outweigh the role, level, and skills failures.
